processing: Small unopened buds, hand-plucked and dried in natural sunlight, which one seller credits for the golden colour.
harvest_season: Hand-picked as unopened buds; no fixed season is well documented, and only a very small quantity is made each year.
appearance_dry: Slender, unopened buds in a pale white-gold.
appearance_liquor: Golden and clear; one seller calls it burnt gold.
appearance_wet: Soft, intact buds in a light golden olive.
taste_profile: Light and softly sweet with florals; tasters also mention hay and pollen, and a tart, slightly drying finish.

brewing.notes: Usually brewed Western-style. Cooler water keeps delicate buds from turning flat; this follows common practice for bud white teas.

vintage_note: Sold in very small lots, often without a harvest date. As with other bud-only white teas, freshness matters, so buy from sellers who state the year and estate.
description:
Ceylon Golden Tips is a white tea from Sri Lanka made from small, unopened buds. Think of silver needle, but with a white-gold colour instead of silver. Sri Lanka's Export Development Board notes it is usually grown at higher altitudes and that very little is made each year.

The method is reported as simple: hand-picked buds dried in sunlight, which one seller says is what keeps their golden colour.

Expect a light, sweet, floral cup with a hay-like note and a slightly tart finish. Do not expect strength. Keep the water below boiling and give the buds a few minutes.

Watch the label. 'Golden tips' is also used for tippy black tea from Ceylon, and one seller places the white version in the Nuwara Eliya district. Check that the tin says white tea and names an estate.
history: Little is documented about when this style first appeared or who developed it. It is sold as a rarity within Sri Lanka's specialty white tea range, and no reliable early date or maker is on record.
